events.title: Trinity's capture and breakout in Room 303
events.summary: Four officers breach Room 303 in the fire-gutted Heart O' The City Hotel and take Trinity at gunpoint; she submits with deliberate slowness. Outside, three Agents strip the Lieutenant of his operation and tell him his two units are already dead. Back in the room, the moment the Big Cop reaches to cuff her, Trinity moves: she kills all four cops in a blur of inhuman speed and stands alone over the bodies, a single curse escaping her.
events.action: The raid succeeds on paper — Trinity is cornered and complies — but the compliance is only the pause before she inverts it. The trigger is not threat but touch: the instant the Big Cop's cuffs reach for her, she breaks the arrest and turns the squad into corpses. Meanwhile the Agents arrive and, without firing a shot, declare the police effort already a failure.

affects_outside.enables: Trinity's clean escape leaves the hotel a crime scene full of dead police and no suspect, forcing the Agents to take over the pursuit directly and setting the story on the path to the rooftop chase.
affects_outside.blocks_or_costs: It ends the police operation as a viable effort — two units are already dead and the room squad is wiped out — so ordinary law enforcement can no longer contain the target and is pushed aside.
affects_outside.off_screen_reactor: The wider police operation and whatever command sent the Agents now face proof that the target is far beyond a 'little girl,' a reckoning the Lieutenant has just been handed in full.

events.turns_on: The moment the Big Cop reaches with the cuffs and Trinity moves — touch, not threat, flips the raid from a clean arrest into a massacre.

carried_uncertainty.what: Whether Trinity surrenders willingly or is setting a trap — her slow compliance is ambiguous.
What Trinity was doing on the computer before the cops entered.
Whether the other three POLICE OFFICERS speak or only the BIG COP.
Whether any cop besides Trinity survives the gunfire.
The precise reason Trinity says "Shit" — whether it is frustration, relief, or something else.

events.boundary_reason: The unit opens with the cops breaching Room 303 and closes once Trinity has turned her arrest into a massacre and stands alone over the dead; the next scene shifts to the Agents arriving outside, answering a new question about who is closing in on her.

events.title: The Agents split to hunt her
events.summary: Outside the Heart O' The City Hotel, the two agents stop approaching as a pair and divide the search: Agent Brown goes into the building while Agent Smith breaks off alone toward the alley, each covering a different route in pursuit of the same quarry.
events.action: The two agents arrive together at the Heart O' The City Hotel and then separate, Brown entering the hotel and Smith turning toward the alley.

positional.entry: approaching the hotel alongside Agent Brown
positional.change: he leaves the shared approach and breaks off on his own toward the alley

affects_outside.enables: Smith's solo move toward the alley sets him on the path to confront her in the alley, while Brown's entry into the hotel keeps the other escape route covered.
affects_outside.blocks_or_costs: The pair lose the safety of moving together, leaving each agent to face whatever is down his own route without backup.
affects_outside.off_screen_reactor: The woman they are hunting is now boxed between two routes, forcing her to commit to one and be exposed to whichever agent holds it.

events.turns_on: The single approach dividing into two separate paths — the hotel and the alley.

carried_uncertainty.what: Which of the two routes she will take, and which agent she will run into.

events.boundary_reason: After the room is cleared, the story pivots to the Agents' arrival and their decision to divide — Brown into the building, Smith to the alley — setting up a fresh pursuit rather than continuing the completed fight.

events.title: Trinity's flight to the exit phone
events.summary: Trinity's planned exit collapses when Morpheus tells her the traced hardline is dead and Agents are on site, so she is redirected to a phone at Wells and Lake. She breaks from the hotel hall moments before Agent Brown and a police unit enter, is forced up the fire escape when Agent Smith holds the alley below, and runs the rooftops where she clears an impossible 40-foot gap — a leap Agent Brown then duplicates, revealing the pursuers break the world's physics too. events.action: Trinity's planned exit collapses when Morpheus tells her the traced hardline is dead and Agents are on site, so she is redirected to a phone at Wells and Lake. She breaks from the hotel hall moments before Agent Brown and a police unit enter, is forced up the fire escape when Agent Smith holds the alley below, and runs the rooftops where she clears an impossible 40-foot gap — a leap Agent Brown then duplicates, revealing the pursuers break the world's physics too. She hurls herself across a 50-foot chasm into a dark building, crashes through a window onto a back stairwell, and, bleeding and broken, keeps moving. Hurt and racing a garbage truck on the street below, she reaches the ringing phone booth and answers it an instant before the truck pulverizes it, vanishing before the Agents can take her — while Agents Smith, Jones, and Brown confirm the informant is real and that they now have the crew's next target: Neo.
participants: the phone at Wells and Lake

physical.entry: Panicked and swearing after learning Agents are present
physical.change: She re-centers on Morpheus's order and commits to the run, then drives herself through an impossible rooftop gap, a window, and a stairwell crash, absorbing real injury without letting it stop her.
physical.exit: On her feet and moving despite being broken and bleeding, answering the phone a split-second before the truck destroys the booth.

knowledge.entry: She believes the hardline is her way out and that the Agents are a terminal escalation.
knowledge.change: She learns the hardline is cut and that she must reach a different phone under Morpheus's direction.
knowledge.exit: She believes the Agents will try to physically stop her and that she can reach the phone first — unaware the informant has already handed them the next target.

status.entry: Cornered in the hotel with a compromised exit and Agents closing in.
status.change: She is hunted through the building and across the rooftops, forced up and over ever more lethal gaps, then cornered again on the street racing the truck to the booth.
status.exit: She escapes the building and the Agents entirely — gone before the booth is destroyed — but only by improvising the desperate run Morpheus named.

safety.entry: Connected to a hardline that she believes is her way out
safety.change: The traced line is cut and Agents arrive, so her safe exit becomes a worsening series of improvisations — hall, fire escape, rooftops, a 50-foot dive, a stairwell crash — until the street itself becomes a kill box.
safety.exit: She answers the phone and is gone before the truck destroys the booth; there is no body and no pursuer left holding her.

state_triples.reading: Trinity runs on trained, coldly managed adrenaline: she has already accepted that the only way across any gap is total commitment, so there is no hesitation to spend. Her calm is not the absence of fear but a decision not to let it touch her hands or her stride — the same self-regulation she showed taking the deep bath

physical.entry: Directing the operation from off-site, his voice her only link to the crew.
physical.change: He confirms the hardline is cut, refuses to answer her fear directly, redirects her to Wells and Lake, and gives the single command to move.
physical.exit: Directing the operation from off-site, his voice her only link to the crew.
physical.unchanged_because: He never enters the scenes physically; he acts only through the line, so his position and condition are unchanged.

knowledge.entry: He already knows the line was traced and the hardline cut before she finishes reporting it.
knowledge.change: He confirms the cut, names a reachable exit, and asserts confidence that she can make it.
knowledge.exit: He already knows the line was traced and the hardline cut before she finishes reporting it.
knowledge.unchanged_because: He is ahead of her information throughout and gains nothing new; his role is to impose steadiness, not to learn.

status.entry: The guiding authority steering Trinity past panic toward a reachable exit.
status.change: He forces her past the blow, supplies the destination and the encouragement, then the command to go.
status.exit: The guiding authority steering Trinity past panic toward a reachable exit.
status.unchanged_because: His function as commander is constant across the one scene he is in; he neither rises nor falls within it.

safety.entry: Safe off-site, but working against a clock he can see better than Trinity can.
safety.change: He loses the hardline and must route her through a far riskier exit under pressure.

events.title: Neo is summoned and drawn toward the truth
events.summary: Alone in his technology-choked apartment, Neo is woken by his own screen typing back at him with a series of messages that name him and command him to follow a white rabbit; a real knock answers the last line, and the visit of a drug buyer ends with Neo shaken and unable to trust cause and effect. When he spots a small white rabbit pin on Dujour's jacket, the room tilts and he abandons his refusal to go out. Drawn to a crowded, black-clad gathering, he is met by name by Trinity, who confirms she
events.action: was on his computer, warns him that he is in danger and being watched, reframes his sleepless solitude as the mark of a seeker, and presses her body to his as she tells him the answer he chases cannot be told but must be seen. Neo voices the question aloud — 'What is the Matrix?' — and is told the answer is out there, looking for him, before she melts into the crowd and a rising sound closes over him.

affects_outside.enables: It sets Neo in motion toward the resistance: he now carries the question and the warning that will lead him to the phone, the bug, the extraction, and Morpheus.
affects_outside.blocks_or_costs: It ends his ordinary, insulated hacker's life — the 'This never happened. You don't exist' world Choi represents is about to be voided, and his anonymity is no longer available to him.
affects_outside.off_screen_reactor: The Agents, who already have his name and are closing in; Trinity's gamble that she had time to finish the pitch is a gamble against their approach, and the rising sound that closes over Neo hints at the surveillance tightening around him.

events.title: Neo's failed escape from Meta CorTechs
events.summary: Across four linked beats, Neo's ordinary life is breached and then collapses. Waking late and alarmed, he endures Rhineheart's ultimatum with detached, surface-level compliance. A delivered phone connects him to Morpheus, who warns that 'they' are coming; Neo watches the Agents and cops close in, then obeys a turn-by-turn escape through the cubicle maze. Cornered in an empty office, he is told to cross a scaffold to the roof, commits to the ledge, but his nerve breaks when the wind hits and the
events.action: The event converts Neo from a self-contained hacker into a hunted fugitive who must trust an unseen guide, and it does so by stripping away every layer of his ordinary world in sequence — sleep, job, anonymity, and finally his one escape route. The through-line is the transfer of agency: he stops questioning and starts obeying, yet that very obedience cannot carry him across the ledge, because his terror of the height blinds him to the fact that retreat means capture by forces whose intentions Morpheus himself cannot name. His failure at the physical test is what delivers him into enemy hands and sets the interrogation in motion.

physical.entry: Shaken, his grip on the boundary between the digital and the real no longer solid, standing alone in a crowd awaiting a sound that swallows him.
physical.change: He is dragged from sleep, submits to a workplace reprimand, is physically overwhelmed by the raid, and finally collapses back from the ledge after the wind knocks him off balance.
physical.exit: Exposed and nearly lost on the building's face, having retreated inside at the last moment as a cop opens the door.

knowledge.entry: He has spoken the question 'What is the Matrix?' and been told the answer exists and will find him, but cannot be told — a seeker with a question and no answer.
knowledge.change: Curiosity about the mysterious caller gives way to the reality that organized forces are closing in on him for reasons he cannot fathom.
knowledge.exit: Confronted with a lethal pursuit he does not understand, demanding to know who is coming and what they want.

emotional.change: Detachment and hesitation give way to decisive obedience under Morpheus's commands, then shatter at the ledge when the physical risk becomes real.
emotional.exit: Terrified and retreating, convinced the crossing is impossible and that he is being punished for no reason.

affects_outside.enables: Neo's failure at the ledge delivers him into the Agents' custody, which sets the interrogation-and-physical-modification sequence in motion and forces the resistance to intervene.
affects_outside.blocks_or_costs: It costs Neo his last clean exit and his remaining illusion that he can stay uninvolved; the self-directed escape he could have controlled is gone, and the path ahead will be chosen for him under duress.
affects_outside.off_screen_reactor: Morpheus, though present only as a voice, will have to respond to the failed extraction by pursuing a riskier rescue — and the Agents, having closed the net, will move to process their prisoner.

events.turns_on: Neo's nerve breaking at the ledge — the moment fear overrides obedience and he climbs back inside rather than take the one exit Morpheus vouched for.

carried_uncertainty.what: Why Neo is alarmed at 9:15 A.M. and what he is late for.
Whether any character is meant to be present in the skyscraper slug, and the time of day it depicts.
Whether Neo's 'Perfectly clear' is genuine compliance or concealed resentment, and whether RHINEHEART would fire him immediately or merely warned him.
Whether the female employee who points out Neo's cubicle acts knowingly or incidentally, and what the Agents specifically intend to do to him.

Whether Neo is truly in danger of dying from the height or whether it is an illusion within the Matrix; who 'they' are beyond the Agents and cops; and whether the cop who opens the door has already spotted him.

events.boundary_reason: The next morning's lateness, Rhineheart's ultimatum, and Morpheus's guided flight through the office form one unit of attempted escape that ends when Neo's nerve breaks on the ledge and he climbs back inside to be caught — a different question than the chase itself.

events.title: Neo is taken and interrogated by the Agents
events.summary: The Agents drag a handcuffed Neo out of the skyscraper and into a dark sedan while Trinity watches from her motorcycle and reacts with dismay. In the interrogation room, Agent Smith lays out Neo's two lives from a file and offers to erase his crimes in exchange for help hunting Morpheus. Neo refuses with contempt, demanding his phone call, so Smith drops the pretense of negotiation, seals Neo's mouth shut, and has the other Agents pin him while a wire-tap animates into a creature and burrows in.
events.action: The Agents seize Neo and force him into the sedan; Smith moves from a courteous pitch to physical enforcement, sealing Neo's mouth and implanting a wire-creature.

physical.change: Defiance is answered by physical violation: his mouth seals shut and a creature burrows into his body.
physical.exit: Mouthless and implanted — his lips meld into smooth skin and a wire-creature worms into his navel.

events.title: Neo chooses to meet Morpheus and is taken by the crew
events.summary: Waking from a nightmare that may or may not have been real, Neo is pulled by a ringing phone into a brief, tapped conversation with Morpheus, who names him 'the One' and extracts a single 'Yes' before directing him to the Adams Street bridge. On the rain-soaked bridge, Trinity pulls up and orders him into the car. events.action: He bolts upright screaming, checks his mouth and stomach to confirm they are normal, then the ringing phone 'almost stops his heart.' His only lines are 'The Agents —', 'What the hell is happening to me?', and the hesitant '... Yes,' after which he closes his eyes unsure of what he has done.

events.action: In the moving car, Neo is made to strip and lie back while Trinity seals an extraction device over his navel and Switch feeds it power from the cigarette lighter. Told he is bugged, Neo endures the machine sucking at his stomach and, when the ultrasound monitor shows the parasite shifting, Trinity escalates to an electric charge that convulses him until the bug is driven out through the coils. She displays the writhing thing in a glass cage, then rolls down the window and drops it; it hits the pavement and reverts into an ordinary wire tap as the car disappears into the rainy night.

events.title: Arrival at the Lafayette and the Red Pill
events.summary: The crew's car comes to rest in a deserted alley behind the Hotel Lafayette, and the operation moves inside. Trinity leads Neo along the thirteenth-floor hall to room 1313, warns him to be honest because 'He knows more than you can possibly imagine,' and leaves Neo alone with Morpheus. Morpheus reframes Neo's lifelong unease as knowledge of a hidden system, names it 'the Matrix,' and offers a final choice: the blue pill ends the story in comfortable ignorance, the red pill means staying to learn
events.action: the truth. Neo swallows the red pill. In the next room the crew wires Neo up as Morpheus explains the pill is a trace program to pinpoint his location; the mirror liquefies and crawls into Neo's body, his vitals fail, and just as Apoc locks his target Morpheus orders the signal sent, driving Neo into cardiac arrest before everything is swallowed by darkness.

affects_outside.enables: Neo's unplugging: the trace program and Apoc's lock hand his real-world body's location to the crew, setting up his awakening in the pod and the wrecking of his lifelong assumption that the world is real.
affects_outside.blocks_or_costs: The easy return is closed — the blue pill is refused and Morpheus has broken a rule to free an older mind, so the only path now is forward into the cost of the truth; Neo nearly dies on the table, the real price of the freedom he asked for.
affects_outside.off_screen_reactor: Tank, summoned by Morpheus's call for 'the signal,' must now send it; and the Oracle's world — the 'He' who 'knows more than you can possibly imagine' — has just lost a potential threat as Neo is marked and pulled out.

events.turns_on: Neo swallowing the red pill — the self-chosen, irreversible crossing that turns a fan meeting into an extraction and converts a named idea into a bodily catastrophe.

carried_uncertainty.what: Whether 'He' refers to the Oracle or someone else.
The exact time of day.
Whether Neo survives the arrest or what exactly lies in the darkness he is swallowed into.
Whether the mirror's liquefaction is a physical event in the room or a manifestation inside Neo's perception of the Matrix.
What 'Tank' and 'the signal' concretely are beyond Morpheus's call for them.

events.boundary_reason: The car stopping behind the hotel begins the approach to Morpheus, the choice of pills, and the trace that locates Neo; swallowing the red pill and being tracked down through the liquefying mirror is one continuous action that ends when the signal fires and Neo is swallowed into darkness.

events.title: Waking in the Pod and Recovery
events.summary: Neo ruptures the shroud of his pod and learns he is one of countless farmed humans, only to be disconnected by a machine and sucked into a black hole; he is then flushed through waste lines, nearly drowns, is snatched up by a cable into a flying machine, and is set down inside a hovercraft where Morpheus names him and the real world before he passes out.
events.action: The man in the pod tears free of the gelatin shroud, discovers the coaxial locked into his skull and the endless ranks of other farmed bodies, and is seized by a machine that unlocks and unplugs him before a vacuum drags him into a black hole. He falls and slides through a waste pipe, is flushed up through grease traps, begins to drown in the sewer main, and is snatched from the flow by a metallic cable into a hovering flying machine. Inside the hovercraft the harness opens, human hands and arms lift him up, and Morpheus welcomes him to the real world by name before he collapses.

events.title: Waking Aboard the Nebuchadnezzar
events.summary: Neo wakes aboard the hovercraft and is carried from a mythic arrival through physical rebuilding to an ontological shock. Morpheus, certain they have found the one they sought, greets the half-conscious Neo, then oversees the repair of his atrophied body while doling out only enough truth to keep him calm. Once Neo is awake and examining the hardware grafted into his own flesh, Morpheus stops explaining and reframes the crisis as one of time — revealing Neo has lost roughly two centuries — and,拒

events.title: The Construct and the Desert of the Real
events.summary: Morpheus jacks Neo into the Construct and, over a guided descent through the history of the war and the horror of the human battery farms, lays out the full truth of the Matrix; Neo's mind refuses to take it in and his body violently ejects him back to the ship, where he collapses.
events.action: On the main deck, Morpheus introduces Neo to the crew and the Core, then has Trinity seat him and feeds a coaxial line into the jack at the back of Neo's neck until a CLICK fires and Neo drops into weightlessness. He wakes in the blank-white Construct, where Morpheus reframes 'real' as signals the brain reads, shows him the Twentieth-Century world as the Matrix and the ruined world of today as 'the desert of the real,' and spirals their viewpoint down to a scorched lake bed while recounting mankind's birth of A.I., the scorched sky, and the resulting dependence on machines. The feed then runs through the fetus fields, where a thresher-like farm machine plucks a fetus from its placenta-like husk, and through a power plant where a tiny newborn suckles its feed tube — Morpheus explaining that humans are grown, not born, and that he only believed the truth once he saw the efficiency. Back in the Construct he clicks off the television, defines the Matrix as control, and holds up a coppertop battery as the symbol of what humans are reduced to. Neo shouts that it is not possible and demands to be let out; Morpheus refuses. Neo then tears free on the main deck as Trinity unlocks the cable,

events.title: The Prophecy of the One
events.summary: In his dark room, Neo asks whether he can go back; Morpheus, sitting like a shadow in the corner, says no and asks whether he would truly want to. Morpheus apologizes, explaining the rule against freeing a mind past a certain age and admitting he broke it because he had to. He then recounts the origin myth of a man who could remake the Matrix, the Oracle's prophecy of his return to end the war, and finally reveals his own conviction that 'the search is over' before standing, telling Neo to rest,
events.action: Morpheus reframes Neo's rule-breaking rescue as destiny: he pairs an apology for freeing an older mind with the myth of the One and the Oracle's prophecy, then commits to guiding Neo into 'your training.' Neo stops resisting and accepts, in resignation, that there is no return.

events.title: Morning and the Operator

Tank then defines Zion as 'the last human city,' deep underground near the earth's core, lets his excitement about Neo's potential leak through, and pivots to work.

events.title: I Know Kung Fu
events.summary: Tank loads combat programs straight into Neo, skipping the boring basics, and Neo goes from disbelief to giddy possession of the skills. After ten hours of downloads, he declares that he knows kung fu, and Morpheus arrives to turn that claim into a test. In the sparring program Morpheus teaches that the simulated rules can be bent and broken, then dismantles Neo's furious assault with effortless ease. Beaten to the floor and spitting blood, Neo blames Morpheus's speed until he is pushed to admit
events.action: that even the air isn't real. Still outmatched, Neo is driven by rage to finally land a clean blow that knocks Morpheus's glasses off. Afterward Morpheus reframes himself as only a guide who can show the door, tells Neo he must step through himself, and orders Tank to load the jump program. On the main deck the crew watches the fight like a game and Mouse marvels at Neo's off-the-charts neural-kinetics.

events.title: The Jump
events.summary: In the Construct, Morpheus demonstrates the rooftop jump and coaches Neo to free his mind; Neo forces himself to run but fails the leap and falls, then names his disbelief as the cause. On the main deck the crew watches the attempt split between doubters and a hopeful Trinity, and after Neo is pulled out injured, Morpheus converts the failure into the doctrine that the mind makes the Matrix real and death there kills the body. Tank handles the physical recovery while the rest of the crew argues,
events.action: Morpheus crosses the gap in the Construct to prove the jump is possible, then Neo steels himself and runs but falls short and is caught by the program's yielding ground; the crew watches on a screen and, once Neo is unplugged and spitting blood, Morpheus states that the mind makes the Matrix real and that death there kills the body, while Tank eases the plug and helps both men.

events.title: The Agent Training Program
events.summary: Morpheus walks Neo through a frozen downtown street that turns out to be a training program, not the Matrix, and uses it to teach the rules of survival: the people inside the system are enemies until freed, Agents are sentient programs that can inhabit anyone still plugged in, and every human who has fought one has died. events.action: Morpheus leads Neo through a crowded downtown street that is actually a training program. He explains that the Matrix is a system that is their enemy, and that the ordinary people inside it are still part of that system and therefore enemies. When Neo gets distracted by a woman in a red dress, Morpheus reveals the danger: the crowd can become Agents. Neo turns to find Agent Smith leveling a gun at his face, and he screams. Morpheus freezes the program, then teaches that Agents are sentient programs who can inhabit anyone not yet unplugged, and that every human who has fought one has died — but Neo will succeed because their strength and speed are bound by rules, whereas Neo's are not. When Neo asks if this means he can dodge bullets, Morpheus says that when he is ready, he won't have to. The lesson is interrupted when Morpheus' cell phone rings and Tank reports trouble.

events.title: The Sentinel Attack and the E.M.P. Wait
events.summary: A Sentinel is picked up sweeping in on the Nebuchadnezzar, and Morpheus orders the ship hidden in a tight supply line while the crew runs the E.M.P. drill: power goes dark, the machine glides over them in silence, and once it passes they finally breathe.
events.action: The Nebuchadnezzar blisters through a sewer main and then sets down, wedged into a pipe barely its size. In the cockpit, Morpheus learns the warning came from another ship, Big Brother, not Zion; an alarm sounds and Dozer reports a Squiddy sweeping in, so Morpheus orders the ship set down. Neo learns from Trinity and Dozer that a Squiddy is a Sentinel, a search-and-destroy machine. Morpheus hails Tank over the intercom; on the main deck Tank kills the turbines, reports power offline with the E.M.P. armed, and curls his fingers around the glowing red key. Back in the cockpit, Trinity explains the E.M.P. to Neo, Dozer says they wait, the heating dies and the cockpit freezes, and Morpheus stops Neo from moving because the machine will hear him. Dozer clears frost from the windshield, the crew sees the machine glide over them and vanish, and only then does everyone breathe easier.

state_triples.reading: The crew moves as one body through the drill — silent, frozen, waiting — and the machine's passage is felt rather than fought. Their arc is the event's spine: from tense exposure, through the physical cost of the cold and the knowledge of seeing the hunter, to the collective exhale when it is gone. That relief is real,

affects_outside.enables: The E.M.P. stays armed and unused because the machine passes without triggering it, so the ship survives to keep moving and Neo's education in the real war continues. Morpheus's bet that Neo will obey on command is confirmed, deepening the trust he will keep
affects_outside.blocks_or_costs: The evasion burns time, power, and heat — the ship is left cold and dark, and any pursuit or schedule it had is interrupted. The crew survives by hiding rather than fighting, which costs them the illusion that the training program was the whole of the war.
affects_outside.off_screen_reactor: Big Brother's crew, running the parallel pipeline, is the off-screen source of the false warning that set this evasion in motion; whether they survived their own Sentinel is not shown here. Tank's report over the intercom implies a ship-wide response belowde

events.boundary_reason: The ship's wake, the alarm, the order to hide, the crew freezing in silence while the machine passes, and their relief form one continuous survival sequence; the next scene settles the ship into quiet sleep, ending the threat.

events.title: Cypher's Late-Night Undermining
events.summary: After the ship falls silent and dark following the Sentinel scare, Cypher holds the main deck alone at the operator's chair until Neo joins him. Over drinks poured from Dozer's jug, Cypher turns a friendly debrief into a quiet campaign against Morpheus: he mocks the 'save the world' mandate as a mindjob and tells Neo that five candidates before him all died taking on an Agent because Morpheus filled them with belief in bullshit. Neo, initiated and rattled, takes the warning as caution and slips
events.action: The ship goes quiet and dark with everyone asleep in the hall, then on the main deck Cypher is startled by Neo approaching the operator's chair. He explains that the screens show the encoded Matrix because there is too much to decode, jokes that he wishes he had taken the blue pill, and pours them both shots of Dozer's liquor. When Neo confirms he is there to save the world, Cypher calls it a mindjob and, under cover of 'don't tell him I told you this,' reveals that Morpheus has believed he found the One five times before and that all five are dead, killed after taking on an Agent. He advises Neo to run from any Agent, and Neo, red-faced from two shots, thanks him for the drink and heads for the ladder as Cypher wishes him sweet dreams.

events.title: Cypher's Deal with Smith
events.summary: At an upscale restaurant, Cypher savors a steak he openly admits does not exist, declaring 'Ignorance is bliss' while Agent Smith presses him for a decision. Cypher lays out his terms — no memory of his real life, and reinsertion into the Matrix as someone rich and important, 'like an actor' — and Smith promises whatever he wants. In exchange, Cypher offers his body returned to a power plant and himself reinserted, and in return he will deliver what Smith wants. Smith names it: the access codes.
events.action: Cypher and Agent Smith finalize a betrayal bargain in a restaurant: Cypher commits to handing over Morpheus in exchange for being reinserted into the Matrix as a wealthy, forgetful, important man, and Smith names the objective as the access codes to the Zion mainframe.

events.title: The Decision to Visit the Oracle and the Jump-In
events.summary: During a gray-protein breakfast, Morpheus breaks into the crew's banter, orders twelve-hour standby, declares 'we're going in,' and singles Neo out to be taken to see 'her'—whom Tank then names for Neo as the Oracle. Tank launches the flight from the operator's station, the crew is driven forward under acceleration, and the jump resolves with the whole crew materializing in the empty Hotel Lafayette room as Morpheus answers the ringing phone and confirms they are in.
events.action: The crew eats in the mess hall while Mouse brags about writing the Agent training program and offers Neo a private encounter with a woman he designed, drawing mockery from Apoc and Switch while Dozer explains the food and Tank looks after Neo. Morpheus enters, issues the standby order and the mission, and leaves without explaining 'her'; Tank supplies the name 'the Oracle' to Neo. The scene shifts to the Main Deck, where Tank strikes the enter key to start the flight. The jump carries the crew into the construct, landing them in the Hotel Lafayette room where Morpheus answers the phone.

events.title: The Door and the Waiting Room
events.summary: Morpheus leads Neo down a dark hall to a door he can only point at, and Neo recoils, insisting he believes in nothing since his whole world was a lie. When Neo taunts him about the five who came before, Morpheus drops his doctrine and admits he misunderstood the Oracle, thought the prophecy was about himself, and was terribly wrong, losing his way after the fifth until he saw Neo. Offering only his own hard-won faith and asking Neo to trust him on credit, he wins Neo over, and Neo agrees to step
events.action: through. The handle turns on its own, a woman in white opens the door, and greets Neo as right on time. In the Oracle's apartment the Priestess tells Morpheus to make himself at home and leads Neo away to a family room of Potentials. Left waiting, Neo sits with a Spoon Boy who hands him a straight spoon and teaches him not to try to bend it but to realize there is no spoon, so only oneself bends. As Neo stares and the room reflected in the spoon begins to warp, the Priestess touches his shoulder and announces the Oracle will see him now.

events.title: The Oracle's verdict
events.summary: In the Oracle's kitchen, Neo is told he is not the One but has 'the gift' and is waiting for something, then handed a lethal choice: Morpheus believes in him so blindly he will die for him, and Neo will decide which of them lives. The Oracle steadies his panic with a cookie and the insistence that he controls his own life. In the sitting room, Morpheus escorts him out, treats what passed as private, and offers to keep it secret; Neo accepts, still eating his cookie.
events.action: The Oracle confirms Neo is not the One, loads him with the prophecy that Morpheus will die to save him and that he alone will choose who dies, then calms his physical panic with reassurance and a cookie; afterward Morpheus greets him as one who has received a private word and offers to guard it.

events.title: The uneasy ride back to the exit
events.summary: The crew breaks from the Oracle's apartment and moves toward extraction. In the car, Cypher probes for the verdict and is shut down by Morpheus, then Neo deflects Trinity's worry with a false all-clear. Meanwhile Tank warns Mouse that the crew is inbound, and on arrival Cypher's easy grin curdles into visible nerves. The event is a single held breath: a secret kept from the wrong person, a lie told to the right one, and an approaching threat the group does not yet feel.
events.action: Neo and Morpheus enter the car where Cypher waits in the driver's seat. Cypher asks for the Oracle's news; Morpheus cuts him off and Cypher drives in silence. Trinity asks Neo if he is all right; he eats the last of his cookie and claims to be 'right as rain.' In ROOM 1313, Mouse answers his ringing phone with a joke and Tank relays that 'they're on their way.' On a city street, the group exits the car; Cypher greets Neo, then follows the others into the hotel while glancing around and wiping sweat from his brow.

events.title: The trap is sprung and Mouse is killed
events.summary: The crew's exit up the Hotel Lafayette stairs is tripped by a glitch that Tank, on the main deck, reads as a deliberately set ambush: someone has cut the hardline and rewritten the building against them. Morpheus gets the group moving and armed while, in Room 1313, Mouse is warned too late, finds the windows bricked up, and is gunned down — his death registering first as a scream on the stairs, then as a flatline on the main deck.

events.title: The crew realizes they're trapped and Morpheus calls for the building's layout
events.summary: The escape stalls when Morpheus hears police massing below, and the group discovers the eighth-floor windows are bricked up. As boot-steps close in, Morpheus seizes Trinity's phone despite her warning that it can be tracked, then demands a structural drawing from Tank, driving a rapid schematic relay toward the main wet-wall. Meanwhile the police sweep the Hotel Lafayette floor by floor, and Agent Smith reports Mouse's death to his unit.
events.action: The crew's flight turns into a cornering: they run down the stairwell and along the eighth-floor hall, find the windows bricked up, and hear boot-steps closing. Morpheus overrides Trinity's objection and takes her phone, then orders Tank to pull the building's structural drawing and, once it appears, to locate the main wet-wall. Off on the ship, Tank feeds him the schematics as the police search the Hotel Lafayette and Agent Smith signals his fellow Agents over Mouse's body.

events.title: Guided to the escape hole and the crew descends inside the wall
events.summary: Tank guides Morpheus blind through Room 808 to the exact spot of the escape opening, and the crew slips into the wall to descend the plumbing stack. On the floor above, Smith's line dies and he relays the crew's eighth-floor position to Brown; boots and cops then flood the eighth floor and sweep Room 808, where they find the room empty and a man-sized hole smashed through the bathroom wall — the crew already gone and concealed inside it.
events.action: Tank directs Morpheus one last step — left, then the destination directly ahead — and Morpheus confirms arrival. The crew enters the wall and worms down the grease-black stack pipes, light still filling the hole above them. Meanwhile Smith's call drops dead and he reports the targets are on the eighth floor; Brown listens in the stairwell as boots climb and cops pour onto the floor and through Room 808, discovering the empty room and the hole in the bathroom wall.

events.title: The Agents find the jacket; a cop discovers the fugitives in the walls
events.summary: Two search fronts converge on the same hiding place. In the hall, Agent Brown and Agent Smith locate Morpheus's abandoned jacket, and Brown openly demands where the escapees are. Meanwhile, in ROOM 608, the cops search in silence until one of them catches a strange sound by the bathroom, presses his ear to the plaster, and—after the wall bulges and shatter-cracks—realizes the fugitives are concealed inside the structure itself.
events.action: Agent Brown and Agent Smith stand over Morpheus's jacket in the hall and Brown demands where 'they' are. In ROOM 608 the cops search silently until one of them hears something strange near the bathroom; he leans his ear against the plaster, hears whispers, hisses and a grunt, and when the wall bulges and shatter-cracks he exclaims that the fugitives are in the walls. Inside the plumbing wall, Cypher has slipped and is wedged between the wall and several thick supply pipes.

events.title: Firefight in the wall and the group fights down to the basement exit
events.summary: The crew's exchange of gunfire with the Cop collapses into a flight down through the building. An Agent ambushes Neo in the wall and nearly kills him, but Morpheus breaks through and pins it, then sacrifices his own escape so Neo can be gotten out. Trinity obeys against her will and drags the protesting Neo away while the Agent is held; the survivors crash into the basement firefight, where Trinity forces open the catch-basin exit and the group goes down the hole — Cypher vanishing into the gas,
events.action: The Cop opens fire inside the wall and Trinity pulls Cypher clear while Neo arms himself and blasts back through the plaster. The Cop, wheeling for cover in the next room, is seized mid-movement — his body spasms and his rifle drops. In the wall, an Agent smashes through and throttles Neo against the iron stack pipe; as its grip closes, Morpheus dives through the wall onto it and pins it before it can reach its weapon. Morpheus orders Trinity to get Neo out because 'he is all that matters,' and when she resists he escalates to a command. Trinity relays the order to Apoc and physically drags the struggling Neo down the inside of the wall. The survivors break through into the basement's mechanical room amid a firefight, where Trinity locates and pries open the cover of the catch basin; as the group moves, a gas can bounces near Cypher and he seems to trip and is swallowed by the smoke while the others go down the wet-black hole.

events.title: The survivors regroup and learn Morpheus is alive
events.summary: Trinity climbs out of a manhole onto the street, while on the ship Tank takes two separate calls — Cypher demanding a fast exit, then Trinity identifying herself — and routes Cypher to Franklin and Erie. Out on a back street, Neo, Trinity and Tank (by radio) confirm that Morpheus is alive but being moved, and Trinity pushes for an exit even as the crew is steered toward the man they already distrust.
events.action: Trinity emerges from beneath a manhole cover onto the street. On the ship, Tank answers a call from Cypher, who demands an immediate exit; Tank directs him to Franklin and Erie. Tank then takes a second call in which Trinity identifies herself. On a back street, Neo asks whether Morpheus is alive; Trinity relays the question to Tank, who confirms Morpheus lives but is being moved to an unknown location. Trinity passes the news to Neo, demands an exit, and learns Cypher is near at Franklin and Erie, where Tank had already sent him.

events.title: Trinity and Neo escape and wake aboard the ship
events.summary: In the TV repair shop, Trinity embraces Neo and for one moment they are shut off from the pursuit, until the ringing phone breaks it and Neo reverses their usual order, sending her out ahead of him. The scene then cuts to the ship's main deck, where Trinity wakes from the jack: relief at being safely back floods her, then collapses into grief as she reads Tank's charred body and wordless face and understands that Dozer is gone, and she pulls him into her arms.
events.action: Trinity throws her arms around Neo in the shop and they stand locked together, alone and alive, until the phone rings. Neo breaks the hold and tells her to go first, sending her out ahead of him. Aboard the ship, Tank unplugs Trinity and her eyes open on the sight of the ship with a surge of relief. She sees his charred wounds and tells him he is hurt; he says he will be all right. She asks after Dozer, and when Tank's face tightens without a word, she takes him into her arms.

events.title: Smith's Conviction and the Crew Re-entering the Matrix
events.summary: Two fronts close around the same captured man. In the Executive Office, Smith first delivers his verdict that humanity is a disease and the Agents are the cure, then, after the serum fails, he sheds his fellow Agents and confesses a private loathing of the Matrix before torturing Morpheus for Zion's codes. events.title: The rescue of Morpheus
events.summary: Trinity finishes downloading the ability to fly a helicopter and declares the team ready to move. Neo then drops a helicopter into view over the Executive Office and rakes it with a .50 machine gun, killing Agents Jones, Brown and Smith in seconds. With the room cleared, he turns his attention to the unresponsive, bound Morpheus and prepares a rope to extract him. As Morpheus recovers and bolts for the window, a revived Smith fires a sweeping line of bullets that wounds Morpheus in the leg, and,
events.action: Trinity absorbs the ability to fly a military helicopter and says let's go. Neo drops a helicopter into view over the Executive Office and fires a mounted .50 machine gun through the windows, killing Agent Jones first, then Agent Brown while he is still firing, and finally Agent Smith. He then stares at the unresponsive Morpheus and shouts for him to get up, before grabbing a climbing rope and attaching one end to his harness. Morpheus comes to, snaps his handcuffs and runs for the window as two Agents enter the adjoining room; Agent Smith screams and fires a sweeping line of bullets that buries one in Morpheus's leg, knocking him off balance. Neo judges that Morpheus won't make the leap, snaps the other rope-end onto a bolted bar, and hurls himself into the open space, colliding with the falling Morpheus before the line snaps taut and Morpheus tumbles free; Neo snatches hold of Morpheus's still handcuffed wrist and cries gotcha.

events.title: The helicopter crash and regrouping on the roof
events.summary: Under Agent Smith's fire, Trinity crash-lands the dying helicopter on a rooftop, freeing Neo from its dragging cord just before it explodes; the crew survives exposed. On the roof, Morpheus reads the impossible rescue as proof of the One and seals the prophecy against Neo's half-formed correction, while Trinity answers his question with a look; Morpheus and Neo then reach Tank, who has already wired an exit at the subway, State and Balbo.
events.action: The helicopter crash and regrouping on the roof spans the doomed landing, the rooftop reckoning, and the call to Tank. Trinity guides the shot-up machine to the nearest roof and, as its rope yanks Neo toward the edge, cuts the cord one-handed before the craft smashes into a glass skyscraper; she swings and bounces against a shatterproof window that spider-cracks. Tank, watching from the Main Deck, exclaims that 'He's the One.' On the roof, Neo pulls Trinity into a shaking embrace and tries to report the Oracle, but Morpheus cuts him off at 'she told me --', reframes the words as exactly what Neo needed, and delivers the 'knowing a path and walking a path' lesson; Trinity answers 'Do you believe it now?' only by looking at Neo. Morpheus then phones Tank for an exit and is told one is ready at the subway, State and Balbo, before the crew moves out.

events.boundary_reason: The doomed helicopter is shed, the trio survives on a rooftop, confirms Neo's identity, and arranges an exit. The next scene shifts to the Agents, who have traced them and are launching a strike — a new phase of pursuit.

events.title: The Agents order the strike; Smith lingers
events.summary: The three Agents burst onto the rooftop to find their quarry already gone, but Brown confirms the trace landed and Jones orders the Sentinels to strike the crew's known position. Smith, sick of their easy confidence, breaks from the unit to the building's edge and insists the targets are still inside. The action then follows the crew to a subway station, where Morpheus exits through a ringing phone, leaving Neo and Trinity behind — while, back on the rooftop, Smith stands fixed in hatred before,
events.action: The Agents charge out onto the rooftop and discover Neo, Trinity and Morpheus have already vanished. Brown reports the trace was completed and Jones declares they have the position; Brown adds that Sentinels are standing by and Jones orders the strike. Smith, unable to stand the exchange, curses and withdraws to the edge, contradicting them with 'They're not out yet.' At the subway station, a phone rings and Neo hustles Morpheus into the booth first; Morpheus answers and disappears, the phone dropping to dangle by its cord. An old man drinking Thunderbird in the shadows watches him vanish, and his eyes widen, glowing white. Back on the rooftop in daylight, Smith stands with his face twisted in hate, convinced he will never be free of the Matrix; he starts to turn away, then something he hears snaps his head back around to stare.

affects_outside.enables: The ordered Sentinel strike sets up the immediate pressure on the crew's exit and, more importantly, fixes Smith's obsession onto Neo — the personal vendetta that will drive their confrontation at the subway and beyond.
affects_outside.blocks_or_costs: The Agents regain the initiative and close off any clean getaway; the crew's margin for escape narrows to a single phone line, and the window before the strike lands is now all that stands between them and destruction.
affects_outside.off_screen_reactor: Tank, holding the crew's line in the real world, is the unseen party who must field Morpheus's arrival and whatever follows, though the scenes do not show him.

events.turns_on: Whether the crew can get out before the ordered strike lands — and whether Smith's refusal to accept their escape proves more accurate than his unit's procedural certainty.

carried_uncertainty.what: Whether the ordered Sentinel strike succeeds, since Smith says "They're not out yet."
Whether Smith's apartness amounts to open opposition or merely private impatience.
What the old man's glowing white eyes signify or whether he is a threat.
Whether Neo, Trinity intend to follow Morpheus through the same phone.

events.boundary_reason: The Agents learn the trio's position and order a Sentinel strike, with Smith breaking from the group. The next scene shows the trio actually reaching and using the exit, answering whether they get out before the strike lands.

events.title: The old man revealed as Smith; Neo trapped
events.summary: Trinity's half-spoken confession in the subway is swallowed by a train that blasts into the station, and in its strobing light the hunched old man in the corner becomes Agent Smith, who fires at Trinity a breath before she jacks out; the shot only shatters the handset's ear-piece. In the hovercraft, Trinity jolts back into her body and, certain Neo is dying, demands that Tank send her back, but Tank says he cannot. Left alone in the station, Neo turns from the wrecked booth to find Smith's gun,
events.action: The ambush breaks the crew's one soft beat and welds the love confession to lethal danger. Trinity is ripped out of the Matrix mid-sentence, leaving her prophecy permanently unfinished, and her terror in the real world crashes against Tank's hard limit: he cannot send her back, so the person most driven to reach Neo is stranded exactly when he is most alone. The reveal of Smith in the old man's guise confirms the hunter tracked them to the phone, and the denied shot — a miss by a fraction — only tightens the trap, ending with Neo cornered, gun on him, addressed by name. The event pivots on Neo's safety: the intimate moment he thought was protected is exposed as the ambush's bait, and he is left with no escape and no backup.

events.title: Neo and Smith's subway battle
events.summary: Neo and Agent Smith exhaust their guns at point-blank range and fire on empty at the same instant, then brawl through the station until an oncoming train interrupts them. Smith pins Neo against the headlight and chokes him, naming the train his death, but Neo refuses the name and fate — declaring 'My name is Neo' — and impossibly hurls Smith into the tunnel ceiling, only for the train to barrel over Smith and leave him bursting from the last car, untouched and still in pursuit.
events.action: The two empty their weapons simultaneously and, when both guns click on nothing, Smith abandons the shootout for hand-to-hand, cutting Neo's forearm and slamming him against steel. Neo answers with a neck-snapping reverse round-house that sends Smith's glasses flying and reveals his ice-blue eyes. Smith vows to enjoy watching him die and pounds him without letup, then, as the train's grinding fills the tunnel, drop-kicks him and forces him into a choke-hold facing the headlight, calling the train the sound of inevitability and his death. Neo, strangling and not ready to die, names himself, surges upward to smash Smith against the concrete ceiling, and backflips free as the train explodes into the station and runs over Smith. Neo, knees shaking, runs for the escalator while the train screeches to a halt and Smith bursts out of the last car in pursuit, his glasses intact.

events.title: The Sentinels Arrive
events.summary: Aboard the hovercraft, Tank loses Neo's feed just as Trinity asks what happened, and Morpheus's attempt to explain is cut off by a siren that sends him to the cockpit. There he reads the sentinels on the hologram radar, sets a five-or-six-minute deadline, and orders Tank to charge the E.M.P.; Trinity objects that it cannot be used until Neo is out, and Morpheus acknowledges her point before insisting Neo will make it.
events.action: The crew's attention shifts from Neo's fight inside the Matrix to the ship's own survival when a siren interrupts Morpheus mid-sentence and drives him to the cockpit. He confirms the sentinel attack on the radar, gives Trinity a five-to-six-minute window, and orders Tank to charge the E.M.P. Tank complies at once; Trinity protests that the weapon cannot be used while Neo is still jacked in, and Morpheus answers that he knows, then reassures her that Neo is going to make it.

events.title: The Chase Through the City
events.summary: Neo snatches a cell phone from a businessman mid-sprint and dials the ship, while the businessman he robbed is revealed to be Agent Smith. Neo reaches Tank by voice and demands immediate extraction; the crew scrambles to route him to an exit as Trinity presses him over the link. Smith closes the distance through the streets and down an alley, then stops, takes aim, and fires — the bullet shattering Neo's reflection in a truck mirror as the pursuit turns into open shooting.
events.action: The chase runs on two intercut fronts — Neo fleeing through the city while the crew works the exit from the hovercraft. Neo takes a businessman's phone and calls Tank, who answers with a flat 'Operator' as Neo begs to be pulled out; Tank keeps searching for an exit while Trinity screams at Neo to get back. On the street, Smith gains ground, and by the alley he has stopped, aimed, and fired at Neo's reflected image.

events.title: The Escape to the Fire Escape
events.summary: Neo is cornered in a crowded market and a dead-end alley, then steered entirely by Tank's voice from the hovercraft as he breaks through a locked door, a wrong apartment door, and a bullet-riddled door to reach a window and the fire escape — with Agent Brown still on him. Tank, reading the Matrix code like a map, converts what he sees into clipped commands and tracks Neo nearly to the fire escape.
events.action: Tank locates an old exit at Wabash and Lake, a hotel, Room 189, then a door and finally the fire escape, barking instructions to Neo. Neo runs the market and alley, kicks in doors on Tank's orders, is corrected to 'his other left,' and leaps for the fire escape as a knife hits the window casing, landing broken and bleeding with Agent Brown behind him.

events.title: Cornered at the Hotel / The E.M.P.
events.summary: Agent Smith halts outside the Heart O' The City Hotel, arrested by recognition of the place, while in the Nebuchadnezzar the crew's attempt to pull Neo out collapses the instant the sentinels arrive. Tank moves to make the call and Morpheus drives him on, but the lights go red, Trinity names the loss, and the ship is struck. Morpheus then throws the lock on the EMP detonator, ready to fire, convinced Neo will still get out.
events.action: Agent Smith stops outside the Heart O' The City Hotel, struck by the place. In the Nebuchadnezzar, Tank loads the exit and commits to making the call while Morpheus orders him on; the lights go red, Trinity says no, Morpheus registers the pursuers' arrival, the sentinels slam down on the ship, and Morpheus opens the lock on the EMP detonator to deploy it.

events.action: Neo climbs a fire escape in an alley while bullets spark and ricochet around him and Agents Brown and Jones close the gap behind him; he then kicks in a window on the third floor and drops into the hall, where the doors count backwards 310, 309. Simultaneously, on the Nebuchadnezzar's main deck, another SYSTEM ALARM sounds, Tank reports that the attackers have burned through the outer hull, and Trinity says 'Hurry, Neo.'

events.title: Grief on the Deck; Trinity's Confession and Kiss
events.summary: On the main deck, Trinity takes hold of Neo's body and speaks his name amid the destruction. In the hall, Agent Brown confirms the vital signs are gone and Agent Smith dismisses the dead man by his real name. Back on the main deck, Morpheus weeps and reaches for the EMP switch while Trinity pleads with Neo, confesses that the Oracle's prophecy means the man she loves must be the One, declares her love twice, and kisses him in full belief that he will feel it.
events.action: Trinity moves from standing apart in the wreckage to physically holding Neo's body and addressing him by name, then to kneeling over him, pleading, and finally kissing him with total conviction. Agent Brown goes from checking vital signs to reporting the death as fact. Agent Smith goes from standing over the body to smiling and bidding the dead man farewell. Morpheus moves from disbelief to tears and to taking hold of the EMP switch, his intent left unresolved as Trinity turns her attention to Neo.

events.action: The sentinels flood the main deck and tear the ship apart. Trinity calls out for Neo. Elsewhere, a man who has been hearing a woman's voice reacts to a ringing phone and runs toward it before the scene breaks. Back on the main deck, a sentinel descends on Morpheus as a screen shows Neo diving for the phone; at Trinity's shout of "Now!", Morpheus turns the key. A blinding shock of white light sweeps the overflow pit, and the sentinels fall dead, their cold metal bodies filling the chamber.

events.boundary_reason: Sentinels overrun the deck, Trinity summons Neo, and on her cue Morpheus turns the key, flooding the overflow pit and killing the machines — the siege ends. The next scene answers what survival and aftermath look like, in stillness.

events.title: Aftermath and Neo's Declaration to the World
events.summary: In the still darkness of the hovercraft, Trinity's vigil breaks: at the sound of her voice Neo's eyes open, and as he reaches up to touch her she weeps with relief and kisses him. The scene then mirrors the film's opening — a cursor beats on a screen, a phone rings and is answered, and a trace program floods the display — while Neo's voice, now heard over the Matrix, tells whoever is listening he is done running and done hiding, and that freedom comes from changing yourself rather than your cage
events.action: Trinity calls Neo's name over his still body; his eyes open and she reaches for her as tears pour from her smiling eyes, then she kisses him. The scene fades and reopens on a computer screen as in the opening, its cursor beating; a phone rings, is answered, and the screen fills with a trace program as Neo's voice addresses the Matrix. Neo hangs up inside a street phone booth, steps out, slides on sunglasses, looks up as the camera rises above the city, then blasts past faster than a speeding bullet, his long black coat billowing like a black leather cape

affects_outside.enables: Neo's open broadcast ends the machines' need to hunt him and reframes the war as a matter of choice, opening the possibility that plugged-in minds can free themselves — the philosophical seed of a future where humans and machines might coexist.
affects_outside.blocks_or_costs: It closes off Neo's life as a fugitive and any return to the old cat-and-mouse dynamic; by declaring himself, he removes hiding as an option for either side.
affects_outside.off_screen_reactor: Whoever answers the ringing phone on the Matrix side — the machines, other plugged-in humans, or both — now hold Neo's voice and his offer, and must decide how to answer it.

events.turns_on: The private resurrection — Trinity calling Neo back and holding the living proof — is what lets the formerly frightened fugitive speak with settled certainty and turn to address the world on his own terms.
